title: Bat and Trap
summary: A pub-garden game of south-east England: a rubber ball rests on a hinged wooden trap, is flipped into the air by a knock of the bat, then struck out across the lawn between two tall posts. The farther it lands inside the field, the more it scores.
howToPlay: Press at the trap, pull back and let go: the bat strikes the ball and sends it up the lawn.
Aim between the two posts; a ball that drifts wide is out of play.
Land the ball in the far strips of grass for the biggest scores. Six strikes make a round, and there are two rounds.
rules: The ball must travel between the two posts; a ball that goes wide counts nothing.
The lawn is marked in strips; the farther the strip the ball lands in, the more it is worth (one to four).
A ball that carries past the end of the lawn is lost.
A light breeze can push the ball sideways, so allow for it.
Each round is six strikes and a game is two rounds; your total decides the stars.
heritageNote: A pub game of Kent and the south coast of England, played on garden lawns and in league matches for generations, with a wooden trap, a solid rubber ball and two tall posts on a pitch measured in yards.
